newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern sets Conrail slate.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern sets Conrail slate.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said it nominated a slate of five directors to serve on the board of Conrail Inc and would seek to remove all but three members of the existing board.
It also proposed reducing the size of the Conrail board to eight from 13 and would seek to eliminate the staggered board system so that all directors would be elected annually.

The move follows Norfolk Southern's recent purchase of 9.9 percent of Conrail shares. Conrail has rejected a $10.3 billion takeover offer from Norfolk Southern in favor of a proposed $9.4 billion merger with CSX Corp
Norfolk Southern said it would seek to remove all current Conrail directors except for Daniel Burke, David Lewis and John C. Marous.

The Norfolk slate includes George Butler, retired president of CoreStates Financial Corp ; Stephen Lamb, a partner in the Wilmington, Del, law firm of Lamb & Bouchard; Mary Patterson McPherson, president of Bryn Mawr College; Bernard Watson, chairman of the HMA Foundation in Philadelphia; and Roger Williams Jr, of Philadelphia law firm Dilworth, Paxson, Kalish & Kauffman.
The proposals are to be considered at Conrail's annual meeting on December 19. They were submitted by Norfolk Southern subsidiary Atlantic Investment Co.

Norfolk Southern also said it will start payment Tuesday for the 8.2 million shares of Conrail that were accepted for payment upon expiration of Norfolk Southern's 9.9 percent tender offer at $115 per share. The final proration factor is approximately 12.6 percent for all Conrail shares tendered.
Norfolk Southern plans to soon start a second $115 per-share all-cash tender offer for all of the remaining Conrail shares.

Norfolk Southern has challenged a provision in Conrail's bylaws that require any vote to lift the company's poison pill antitakeover defense plan is only effective if at least two board members are "continuing directors" and a majority of the continuing directors vote to lift. A continuing director is one who was in place in September 1995, or the specifically desginated successor of such a director.

Monday was the deadline for Norfolk Southern to submit a board slate. Norfolk Southern also contends although the three-year terms of Conrail's board members are staggered, the company's by-laws allow the entire board to be replaced at once.
